welcome.title: A librarian for your own files
welcome.lead: Point it at folders you already have. It reads them, indexes them locally, and answers questions with the passage it used sitting next to the answer.
welcome.privateTitle: Your documents stay on this machine
welcome.privateBody: Parsing, embedding and search all run here. Only the question and the retrieved passages ever reach a model you choose — and that model can be a local one.
welcome.citedTitle: Every claim points at a page
welcome.citedBody: Answers carry citations. Click one and the reader opens on the exact span it came from, so a wrong answer is visibly wrong.
welcome.stepsBody: Check your hardware, get the two retrieval models, pick who writes the answers, add a folder.

hardware.title: Your machine
hardware.lead: Defaults come from what is actually here. Everything below is changeable later in Settings → Performance.
hardware.profileGpu: Plenty of VRAM. Models run on the GPU, batches are large, parsing runs wide.
hardware.profileBalanced: Enough memory to keep the retrieval models resident while you work.
hardware.profileCpu: No usable GPU found. Everything runs on CPU with small batches — slower, still correct.

models.title: The two models retrieval needs
models.lead: Both run locally and are small enough to stay resident. Downloads resume where they stopped and are checked against their sha256 before being used.
models.embeddingWhy: Turns every chunk and every question into a vector. Swapping it later means re-indexing.
models.rerankingWhy: Reads the question and each candidate together, then reorders them. This is what keeps answers on topic.

connection.title: Who writes the answers
connection.lead: Retrieval is local either way. This only decides which model turns the retrieved passages into prose.
connection.remoteWarning: The active connection is remote. Your question and the retrieved passages leave this machine when you ask something. Chat shows a banner whenever that is the case.

library.title: Point it at a folder
library.lead: Files are read in place — nothing is copied or moved. Start with one folder; add the rest from the Library whenever you like.

done.title: Set up
done.lead: Ask something in Chat. If an answer has no citation it says so rather than making one up — that is the whole point.
done.documentsBody: The Library shows every file, its status, and why anything failed.
done.citationBody: It opens the Reader on the page the passage came from, with the span highlighted.
done.diagnosticsBody: Process cards, the core's log tail and a debug report you can paste into an issue.
